articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Clears Site in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A major $50 million EVO Entertainment complex is moving forward in downtown Clearwater, Florida, with the site now cleared for construction. EVO Entertainment operates large-format FECs combining bowling, cinema, arcade, laser tag, and dining under one roof. This development signals continued investor confidence in large-scale entertainment destination concepts in secondary markets.

articles.title: Six Flags Fiesta Texas Breaks Ground on World's Longest Family Launch Coaster
articles.summary: Six Flags Fiesta Texas has broken ground on Werewolf Gorge, billed as the world's longest family launch coaster and the park's largest single-attraction investment in its history, set to debut in 2027. The move underscores the regional park sector's strategy of anchoring attendance growth around headline coaster additions. FEC operators should note the emphasis on family-friendly thrill as a key demand driver heading into 2027.

articles.title: Premium Halloween: Six Flags and Warner Bros. Bet Big on Interactive Horror Experiences
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences are investing heavily in premium, interactive horror with The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, signaling a shift toward immersive, ticketed Halloween upsell experiences. The article explores how operators can move large crowds efficiently while delivering high-value seasonal programming. FEC operators running haunted attractions or seasonal events will find actionable insight into premium pricing and crowd management strategies.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's Lee Cowie outlines how AI and data analytics are reshaping ticketing and in-park purchasing, with the overarching goal of removing friction between guests and experiences. The piece connects directly to the growing operator imperative to personalize guest journeys and increase per-capita spend. FEC operators evaluating ticketing or point-of-sale upgrades will find this a useful technology roadmap.

articles.title: InPark Issue 111: Making the Guest Experience Frictionless Across Every Touchpoint
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's latest issue centers on the concept of frictionless guest experiences, covering ticketing, in-park purchasing, and how technology can eliminate barriers between visitors and fun. The editorial vision aligns closely with FEC operator priorities around throughput, upsell, and repeat visitation. Operators looking to benchmark their tech stack against industry best practices will find this issue particularly relevant.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola, Florida
articles.summary: A new Launch family fun center featuring an arcade and trampoline park is coming soon to Davis Highway in Pensacola, expanding the brand's footprint in the Southeast. The opening adds competitive pressure for existing FEC operators in the Pensacola market. It also reflects the ongoing national roll-out of multi-attraction FEC concepts into mid-size metro areas.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Competitive Socializing Portfolio with New Interactive Game Concept
articles.summary: Jora Vision is growing its competitive socializing offerings, developing interactive game experiences designed to broaden the appeal of attractions beyond traditional ride-based formats. Competitive socializing remains one of the fastest-growing segments within the FEC and entertainment venue space. Operators exploring new anchor attractions or supplementary revenue streams should pay attention to this supplier's expanding lineup.

articles.title: 360Golf Smart Mini-Golf System Uses Automated Scoring and Operator Analytics
articles.summary: 360Golf, developed by Holovis, transforms traditional mini-golf into a tech-driven competitive social gaming experience using smart golf balls, sensor tracking, and automated digital scoring. The system layers in gamified elements like SuperShots and bonus challenges to drive replayability and competitive engagement. FEC operators considering mini-golf as an attraction should evaluate this platform for its ability to reduce labor and increase guest dwell time.

articles.title: Six Flags Darien Lake Drops Fright Fest in Favor of Family-Friendly Halloween Programming
articles.summary: Six Flags Darien Lake is discontinuing its two-weekend Fright Fest for 2026, pivoting entirely to family-friendly daytime Halloween events including Kids Boo Fest and an expanded Oktoberfest. The shift reflects a broader debate in the attractions industry about the relative ROI of family-oriented versus scare-focused seasonal programming. FEC operators planning Halloween events can use this as a data point in evaluating their own seasonal audience segmentation.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, generating significant community response. The closure is a reminder of the operational and market challenges that can face even well-established FEC venues over time. Operators and investors should examine the factors behind the closure as a cautionary case study in long-term venue sustainability.

articles.title: Endless Surf and Flowstate Partner to Bring AI-Powered Wave Technology to Surf Parks
articles.summary: Endless Surf and Flowstate have announced a strategic partnership combining customizable wave generation technology with AI-powered computer vision for surf park operators. The integration aims to create a more personalized surfer experience while giving operators richer data on guest behavior and skill levels. As surf parks continue to emerge as FEC-adjacent attractions, this partnership points to where the technology stack for active entertainment venues is heading.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Designing Interactive Themed Experiences
articles.summary: Interactive experience designer Alterface marks its 25th anniversary, reflecting on its legacy of creating shooting and interactive dark ride systems used in themed entertainment venues worldwide. The company's technology underpins interactive attractions found in parks and FEC-adjacent venues globally. For FEC operators considering interactive dark rides or shooting gallery attractions, Alterface represents a key supplier to watch.

articles.title: Indian Amusement Industry Association Calls for GST Reform to Boost Growth
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries (IAAPI) is pushing for GST rationalization to reduce the tax burden on amusement and entertainment venues across India. The association argues that high tax rates are suppressing consumer demand and limiting industry investment at a time when the market shows strong growth potential. While India-specific, this policy development is relevant to suppliers and investors watching emerging FEC markets globally.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Posts Summer 2026 Growth But Faces Margin Pressure from Rising Costs
articles.summary: India's amusement and indoor entertainment sector saw strong summer 2026 attendance growth, but rising operational costs are squeezing profit margins across venues. The dynamic mirrors challenges facing FEC operators in other markets grappling with labor costs and supply chain inflation. Operators and investors tracking emerging markets should note both the growth opportunity and the structural cost headwinds in India.

articles.title: New Family Entertainment Center Opens in Rock Springs, Wyoming
articles.summary: A new family entertainment center has opened in Rock Springs, Wyoming, adding multi-attraction indoor entertainment to a market that has limited FEC competition. New venue openings in smaller markets reflect the ongoing expansion of the FEC format beyond major metro areas. This is a useful data point for operators and franchisors assessing secondary and tertiary market viability.

articles.title: Mr. Putters Expands Indoor Mini-Golf and Entertainment Offerings Across Tampa Bay
articles.summary: Mr. Putters is broadening its indoor entertainment services for families, schools, and corporate clients throughout the Tampa Bay area. The expansion highlights the growing B2B and group sales opportunity for FEC operators offering structured programming beyond walk-in play. Operators looking to diversify revenue through group bookings and educational outreach will find this model worth examining.

articles.title: Why Urban Design Principles May Better Explain Attraction Success Than Experience Design
articles.summary: Industry analyst argues that the performance gap between similar attractions is better explained by urban design principles—how people move, orient, and make choices in space—than by storytelling or architecture alone. The insight challenges FEC designers and operators to think more carefully about circulation, wayfinding, and spatial decision-making in their venue layouts. This is a thought-provoking framework for anyone planning a new build or renovation.

articles.title: Blue Sky Thinking in Attraction Design: Start with 'What If,' Not 'How'
articles.summary: Industry creatives from Forrec and Moment Factory discuss the importance of separating imaginative concept development from technical constraints, arguing that technology should serve storytelling rather than drive it. They also emphasize designing around timeless human motivators—curiosity, connection, wonder—to future-proof attractions. FEC developers and designers will find practical principles here for ideating new experiences that stand the test of time.

articles.title: Kaiqi Group: China's Leading Manufacturer of Play and FEC Environments Expands Global Reach
articles.summary: Kaiqi Group, with over 100,000 square metres of manufacturing capacity and products in 120+ countries, has evolved from a playground equipment maker into a full-service FEC partner offering master planning, IP integration, and operational support. The company's operations-first philosophy and comprehensive service model make it a significant supplier option for FEC operators globally. Operators planning new builds or expansions should be aware of Kaiqi's integrated capabilities.

articles.title: Toverland Launches Europe's Largest Halloween Experience with 170 Scare Actors
articles.summary: Toverland theme park in the Netherlands is staging what it calls Europe's largest Halloween experience, featuring 13 Halloween Nights with 170 scare actors across 6 scare zones and 6 haunted experiences, alongside 17 family-friendly Halloween Days. The dual-track programming—family days and adult scare nights—offers a model for FEC operators looking to maximize seasonal revenue across multiple audience segments. The scale of investment in live entertainment underscores Halloween's continued importance as an attendance driver.

articles.title: LEGOLAND New York's Brick or Treat Returns with Trick-or-Treating and Halloween Characters
articles.summary: LEGOLAND New York Resort is hosting its Brick or Treat family Halloween event through October, featuring trick-or-treating, live entertainment, and themed character meet-and-greets. The event represents a strong example of family-focused seasonal programming that drives incremental visits without alienating core demographics. FEC operators can draw inspiration from LEGOLAND's approach to transforming existing spaces into seasonal experiential overlays.

articles.title: Apex Entertainment Renews Partnership with New England Patriots Kicker Andy Borregales
articles.summary: Apex Entertainment has renewed its community partnership with New England Patriots kicker Andy Borregales and the New England Center for Children, combining sports marketing with charitable outreach. Sports celebrity partnerships are an effective local marketing tool for FEC operators seeking to build brand awareness and community goodwill. This renewal demonstrates how FEC chains can leverage professional sports relationships to differentiate their marketing.

articles.title: Fresno's Former Bed Bath & Beyond Space Gets New Entertainment Tenant
articles.summary: A vacant Bed Bath & Beyond retail space in Fresno, California is being converted into an entertainment venue, continuing the national trend of repurposing big-box retail for FEC and indoor entertainment use. The conversion highlights the ongoing opportunity for FEC operators to capture affordable, high-visibility retail real estate as the traditional retail sector continues to contract. Operators and developers scouting expansion sites should monitor big-box vacancy trends in their markets.

articles.title: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center Turns to GoFundMe as Last Resort
articles.summary: Tornado Terry's Family Amusement Center in the Keller-Roanoke area of Texas has launched a GoFundMe campaign in an attempt to avoid closure, highlighting the financial precarity facing smaller independent FEC operators. The story serves as a cautionary tale about the challenges of competing with larger regional venues and the limits of community goodwill as a business lifeline. Independent FEC operators should take note of the cash flow and capital access challenges that can threaten venue survival.

articles.title: Indoor Play Town Amusement Venue Proposed for Milford, Connecticut
articles.summary: A new Play Town Indoor Amusement facility has been proposed for a site in Milford, Connecticut, adding to the pipeline of new FEC concepts entering the Northeast market. The proposal reflects continued developer interest in converting commercial real estate into family entertainment uses. Local operators in the Connecticut market should monitor this development as a potential competitive entrant.

articles.title: InPark Magazine Issue 111 Explores Frictionless Technology and Premium Halloween Trends
articles.summary: The latest issue of InPark Magazine covers two major themes highly relevant to FEC operators: frictionless guest experience technology and the rise of premium Halloween programming. Feature contributors include accesso on ticketing, Jora Vision on competitive socializing, and a deep dive into Six Flags' investment in licensed immersive horror. This is a recommended read for operators planning 2027 seasonal and technology investments.

articles.title: Pirate Pete's Family Entertainment Venue Sets Grand Opening for September 18
articles.summary: Pirate Pete's, a new family entertainment venue, has announced its grand opening on September 18, adding another entrant to the FEC landscape. New openings of themed family entertainment venues remain a useful signal for operators tracking competitive activity and consumer demand in their regions. The pirate theming aligns with a broader trend of narrative-driven FEC concepts differentiating through immersive environments.

articles.title: Siam Park's Nighttime Summer Event Drives 20% Attendance Increase
articles.summary: Siam Park in Tenerife recorded a 20 percent attendance increase during its eight-week Siam Night summer event, which transformed the water park into a nighttime festival experience. The result reinforces the value of after-hours programming as a strategy for boosting capacity utilization and attracting adults and teens who may avoid peak daytime crowds. FEC and water park operators should consider how after-hours events can unlock incremental revenue from existing infrastructure.
